audit.whatIsWrong: Smoke Screen (W) is described as a blind in whys[1], wants.you[2], report[10] and phases[6].why. Riot's text has it reduce sight range and slow on the initial impact only — there is no blind, so Rumble's Flamespitter damage is NOT zeroed by standing in the cloud.
audit.why: Rumble's Q is a cone that ticks for 3 seconds and is not an auto-attack, so a blind would not touch it even if W had one. What the smoke actually costs him is the vision to keep repositioning so his cone stays on you.
audit.corrected: Smoke Screen cuts his sight and slows on impact; it does not blind. It denies him the repositioning that keeps you inside Flamespitter's cone, and Rumble has no dash to relocate once he loses you.

audit.whatIsWrong: Quickdraw is treated as a two-charge dash ("E out on the second charge") in early and spikes[0].text, and implied in whys[2].
audit.why: Quickdraw is a single dash on 16/15/14/13/12s whose cooldown is only reduced when Graves lands basic attacks. Advice built on a free second dash gets the player killed in Rumble's cone.
audit.corrected: Quickdraw is one dash, 16s at rank 1 down to 12s, refunded only by landing autos. Rumble's own spikes: Flamespitter 10s at rank 1 to 6s, Electro Harpoon two charges on a 0.5s cast, Scrap Shield 6s flat, The Equalizer 130/105/80s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interactions are unstated and the W interaction is wrong (see point 2).
audit.why: Both kits contain terrain-creating abilities that gate this lane and neither page says so.
audit.corrected: The Equalizer and Scrap Shield both create terrain-class zones that block dashes — Quickdraw cannot cross the flame carpet, so never leave your escape on the far side of his R. Graves' 4 bullets cannot pass through units, so Rumble hiding behind his own wave halves your burst; step to his flank before firing. End of the Line detonates on terrain contact, so fight near a wall for both hits.

audit.why: 73.68% winRate on 19 games in the packet.
Scrap Shield is a 6s cooldown — it is NOT a punishable window, which makes the existing 'trade just after he burns it' framing weak, but the text is not factually false.
audit.corrected: The punishable cooldown is Flamespitter (10s at rank 1) and Overheat lockout, not Scrap Shield's 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[3].text writes "His Equalizer"; the ability is The Equalizer.
audit.why: Flagged in packet defects as a probable wrong ability name.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart said Rumble wins levels 2, 3 and first item and 'Skill' at 4-5 and 6, while every why on the same rows argues Graves wins them, and the packet chart reads Graves for rows 1-5.
audit.why: The page rendered a winner that contradicted its own explanation and the packet.
audit.corrected: Rows 1-5 are Graves. Row 0 stays Skill, row 6 stays Rumble on his teamfight scaling.

edits.after: You hit your level 2-3 spike first: E in, cut his sight with W's smoke so he cannot reposition the cone, and the point-blank 4-shell spread out-trades Flamespitter.

edits.after: Full combo online — E in for the shell burst; Quickdraw is one dash on 16s, cut only by your autos, so land them before heat ramps his empowered ticks.

edits.after: E in and dump the point-blank 4-shell spread from his flank — bullets do not pass through units, so never fire through his wave. Quickdraw is one dash on 16s, refunded only by landing autos.

edits.after: The Equalizer carpet is terrain your Quickdraw cannot cross, and it plus Flamespitter melt grouped squishies — bank the lead before ~25 min.

edits.after: Drop W's smoke on him mid-Flamespitter so he loses sight and cannot re-aim the cone, then commit

edits.before: Rumble has no dash and his Flamespitter only out-damages you if you stand in its full cone — so don't. Use your E to dart in, dump the point-blank 4-shell spread, and E out on the second charge before the flamethrower racks up heat ticks; True Grit is stacking MR against his AP the whole trade. Watch his E harpoon — that slow is what pins you in the flames, so bait it or sidestep before you commit. At level 1 he can chip your reload windows with Flamespitter, so concede that screen and wait for your level 2-3 power spike.
edits.after: Rumble has no dash and his Flamespitter only out-damages you if you stand in its full cone — so don't. Use your E to dart in and dump the point-blank 4-shell spread from his flank, never through the wave: your 4 bullets cannot pass through units. Quickdraw is one dash on 16s and only landing autos refunds it, so the exit is earned. Watch Electro Harpoon — two charges, and that slow is what pins you in the flames, so bait it before you commit. At level 1 concede the screen and wait for your 2-3 spike.

edits.before: Your W smoke blinds tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.
edits.after: Your W smoke cuts sight on tower dives and breaks gank pathing — drop it on arrival and turn their 2v1 into a coin flip you win.

edits.before: You out-skirmish but the crit scalers pass you — convert to picks with smoke-screen blinds and R snipes.
edits.after: You out-skirmish, but The Equalizer is a terrain carpet Quickdraw cannot cross — take picks in the open, never across it.

edits.before: - Rumble Scrap Shield: matchup-defining — Shield + speed on demand — trade just after he burns it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E dash for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Scrap Shield is only 6s, so it is never truly down: the real windows are Flamespitter's 10s at rank 1 and his Overheat lockout, when he cannot cast at all. - Quickdraw is one dash, 16s, refunded by autos — budget it, and never spend it across his R.

notes: Level chart rows 1-5 were flipped to Graves in matched full/content pairs: every existing why on those rows already argued Graves wins them and the packet chart agrees, so the page was rendering a winner contradicting its own explanation. Row 0 (Skill) and row 6 (Rumble) left as-is. Smoke Screen was called a blind in four places — corrected to sight-reduction plus impact slow, consistent with the rumble__graves mirror audit. Quickdraw was written as a two-charge dash in three places; it is one dash on 16/15/14/13/12s refunded by landing autos. Added two interactions absent from both pages: The Equalizer creates terrain that blocks Quickdraw, and Graves' 4 bullets cannot pass through units so firing through the wave halves the burst. Scrap Shield's 6s cooldown makes the whole 'wait for Scrap Shield's cooldown' framing that runs through tldr, winCon, loading, focus.text, dosFull and report[5] structurally wrong — I corrected breakdown.cooldowns but left the rest, since rewriting them all would change focus.text and the loading line's whole premise and that is a champion-level call.
